blocks.text:
Upbeat Christmas music.
STOCK FOOTAGE: sweeping views of Philadelphia. The square
outside City Hall decked in holiday flair: a giant Christmas
tree, market stalls, and the iconic ‘I <3 Philly’ sign.

There is so much to do in Philly at
Christmastime. Ice skating in
Dilworth Park. Watching the tree
lighting at City Hall. But my
favorite place of all--

A small but vibrant neighborhood ART CENTER decorated for the
holidays - artisanal wreaths and a holiday-inspired window
display featuring creations by local kids and artists.

--is right here. At the community
art center.

A wall of FESTIVE FINGER-PAINTED art. A BULLETIN BOARD of
holiday art classes. Visitors explore the various galleries.

Because Christmas is all about
community. And Philadelphia is home
to one of the most beloved public
art scenes in the country.
We follow the voice to SHELBY (30s), sporting an Art Center
tee, paint-flecked overalls, and a name badge that reads:
SHELBY – INTERIM DIRECTOR. She speaks with passion as she
shows the Visitors around.

The Art Center isn’t just a place
to admire art or take classes. It’s
where kids foster creativity and
imagination.
Volunteers guide ornament painting. Seniors pinch clay pots.
Artists explain their pieces to interested passersby.

Where seniors find meaningful
connection. And where artists of
all kinds have a home. Which leads
us to...
Shelby guides the Visitors to a large COMMUNITY MURAL
comprised of overlapping green handprints forming the shape
of a CHRISTMAS TREE. Plenty of empty space yet to be filled.

The community canvas! It’s
tradition for every visitor to
leave their creative mark. Because
art is for everyone. Thanks for
visiting, we hope you’ll be back to
create with us!

Shelby offers paintbrushes to the excited visitors and guides
them to a station with green paint.

Shelby empties the donation box, a hopeful smile on her face.
BEVERLY (60s), short bouncing curls, warm positive energy,
wearing an Art Center tee, walks up.

They seemed like a fun bunch!
Shelby’s smile fades as she counts the cash.

Yeah. Now we only need... 500 more
groups like that to make all the
repairs.

Beverly offers a warm smile. Shelby notices a pile of mail
and begins flipping through it when she spots an envelope
stamped CITY HERITAGE OFFICE - FINAL INSPECTION REPORT.
Beverly rushes over.

I’ll just grab that one--
It’s too late. Shelby is already reading the contents.

“If repairs aren’t completed within
ninety days, the building will be
deemed unsafe for occupancy.”
Shelby flips to the next page attached. Looks up, shocked.

I know. I was hoping to have
something worked out before you--

Because, Shelby. You put your life
on hold to run this place when I
got sick. But now that I’ve got my
health back, I want you to get your
life back. This isn’t your problem
to solve.
Shelby looks around the colorful space.

But this place... It’s too
important. There’s too much history
here. We can’t lose it.

This isn’t your responsibility. I
want you to focus on yourself. You
need to get back to your art.

It’s your dream! I can’t think of
anything more important. You should
be painting - traveling the world!
Not stuck here scheduling after-
school papier-mâché classes.
Shelby takes this in. Then shakes her head.

Maybe someday. But right now, my
focus is saving this place. I just
might need a Christmas miracle to
do it...
What did I do to deserve you?

You’re the best mom in the world,
that’s what.
Beverly squeezes Shelby’s shoulder lovingly.

Shelby sets a tub of ART SUPPLIES in the corner.
FOCUS ON - DESK: A small table-top Christmas tree, and framed
photos of Shelby and Beverly - laughing in paint smocks.
Shelby sits down at her desk where a snack and a drink awaits
beside a PAINT PALETTE. An easel and canvas are perched
nearby.
She turns the TV on. The North American Paint Off plays.

INSERT - TV
Upbeat intro music (a la Great British Bake Show Theme.)
CHYRON: THE NORTH AMERICAN PAINT OFF.
NIGEL STAR (50s), the sharply dressed host, steps into frame.
Behind him, a gorgeous, overly saturated landscape.

Welcome back to The North American
Paint Off, where 6 professional and
amateur artists compete for the
title of ‘painter of the year.’
Shelby dips her brush into paint.
AN HOUR LATER
Shelby pulls her brush away from her finished PAINTING.

Submissions are open just one more
day for our upcoming Jingle Bell
Paint Off, where one lucky artist
will have their artwork displayed
in the prestigious National Gallery
and receive a prize of... $50,000!
Shelby’s head whips up, alert.

If you think you have what it
takes, send in your submission!

Shelby sits at her desk, typing on the computer.
INSERT - COMPUTER: THE JINGLE BELL PAINT OFF submission page.
Shelby types her full name - SHELBY SANDERS. She drags in
PHOTOS of her original abstract paintings.
She hesitates for a moment... then hits SEND.

title: EXT. THE KINGDOM OF SERENDOVIA - CASTLE - DAY

blocks.text:
A beautiful but modest castle estate. Raindrops fall on a
lush, unbridled garden.

A paintbrush sweeps across a canvas. Thick, bold strokes of
color. As the painting takes shape, we reveal the painter -
HENRY (30s), dapper and focused, wearing a red velvet robe.
He steps back to admire his painting.
INSERT - PAINTING: a classical realism interpretation of the
rainy-garden landscape.
Henry sighs and sets his brush down.

Henry steps into the ornately decorated parlor. Christmas
wreaths hang beside paintings of former royals. Two people
stand, waiting impatiently:
BECKS (29), dressed in a sharp satin pant suit ensemble and
royal sash, stands with her nose in a book.
The older gentleman, KING GEORGE (60s), wears a formal suit
and kingly sash. He turns and frowns when he sees Henry.
(All speak with UK/EURO accents.)

Henry, we are to dine with the
Prime Minister and fifteen foreign
dignitaries in ten minutes time--

Henry removes the red velvet robe to reveal the perfectly
tailored suit and sash beneath. Henry adjusts his tie.

Hippie hair. Scruffy beard. You
look like a common woodsman--

The people of Serendovia don’t seem
to mind it. In fact, I doubt they’d
even recognize me without it--

This dinner tonight is of paramount
importance. We must ready the world
for your ascension to the throne--

Before dinner, might we discuss my
request to--

You are the Crown Prince of
Serendovia! It is your duty to this
country and to this family to rule!
Becks is far more fit to rule.
Henry holds his hands out: exactly!

You would have me discard centuries
of succession laws just so you can,
what, sit around and paint all day?

Painting is the only thing I’ve
ever felt called to do.

Has anyone of consequence ever paid
to hang one of your paintings? Has
a museum asked for your work? Has
your "calling" amounted to anything
beyond this castle?
Henry goes to say something but stops short.

My point exactly. I will not permit
you to surrender your title and
responsibilities to become a
painter. Unless you can prove art
to be of equal or greater value to
the world than governing a nation.
George laughs. Henry lets this statement wash over him.
Let us not keep company waiting.
Henry watches his father leave the room, lost in thought.

A cozy space with a small Christmas tree in the corner.
Henry tugs his tie loose, shucks off his suit jacket, and
sits on the bench at the edge of his bed.

Turn on TV.
The TV winks on. THE NORTH AMERICAN PAINT OFF plays.

--Jingle Bell Paint Off. One lucky
artist will win the chance to have
their paintings displayed in the
prestigious National Gallery--

Volume up.
The volume does not increase.

Really? What is the point of that?
Henry searches for the TV remote. Finds it beneath his suit
jacket. He points it at the TV, the volume increasing.

--send in your submissions! As
Ossie Davis once said: "Art is a
form of power... it can affect
change." This holiday season, share
your art, be the change you want to
see in the world!

I’m Nigel Star, see you next time
for the Paint Off Christmas
Edition. Hope you’ll pencil us in!
Off Henry’s face. He knows what he has to do.

title: INT. COMMUNITY ART CENTER - DAY - ONE WEEK LATER

blocks.text:
Shelby stands admiring the ever-evolving COMMUNITY CANVAS.
Her phone rings. She picks up to answer

Shelby! Nigel Star, executive
producer and host of The Jingle
Bell Paint Off.

You’ve been selected as one of our
six artists for our special
Christmas season. Congratulations!

I know, it’s all very exciting!
Now, we’ve emailed over your
contract. And Production will send
your travel and accommodation
details. Assuming of course you
accept the offer to be on the show--
Of course, I accept, but I--

Fabulous. We’ll be filming this
season in Hollyfern Valley, a
veritable winter wonderland, I’m
told! Pack for warm weather. Oh,
and be sure to bring something
suitable for a gala. We’ll wrap the
season with a Christmas Charity
Gala. Live audience finale, holiday
festivities, the winner crowned on
stage! It will be a night to
remember.

That sounds amazing. I can’t
believe it...

Believe it Shelby and congrats! See
you next week!

Nigel hangs up.
END INTERCUT/SPLIT SCREEN

Hello? Nigel?
Shelby blinks in shock.

...I’m going to compete in The
Jingle Bell Paint Off.
Beverly places a duffle bag in the trunk.

Shelby grabs the duffle from out of the trunk. Beverly yanks
it away - puts it back in.

Absolutely not. This is your
moment!

But the show films through
Christmas. And I’ve never missed a
Christmas with you before--
Beverly yanks the duffle out of Shelby’s hands and tosses it
in the trunk. She shuts the trunk door.
You are going. You are doing this.

We do really need that prize
money...
Don’t you worry about that. Just

focus on your art and enjoy this
once-in-a-lifetime opportunity!
I wish you could come with me.

I’ll be cheering you on every step
of the way while I hold down the
fort here.  We’ll celebrate
Christmas together when you’re
back.
Beverly wraps Shelby in a hug.
I’m already so proud of you.
Love you sweetheart. Go get em!
Shelby nods and gets into the backseat of the car.

An aerial view of a picturesque winter landscape. Rolling
hills of pine trees laden with snow.

Charming brick buildings. Brightly colored storefronts. Old-
fashioned lampposts festooned with red Christmas bows. Snow
piled on the edge of sidewalks as holiday shoppers walk by.

Shelby stands, holding her bags, outside of a quaint boutique
hotel exuding old European charm.
INSERT - WOODEN SIGN: THE HOLLYFERN HIDEAWAY.
Shelby smiles and inhales the crisp winter air.

Shelby hauls her luggage into the lobby but pauses to gawk at
the Christmas decor. It’s positively drowning in Christmas.
Shelby approaches reception and spots Nigel Star.
Nigel offers his hand. Shelby takes it, beaming.

Nigel Star. I’m such a huge fan! I
can’t believe I’m here right now.

We’re lucky to have you. You’re
quite the talent! Now, let’s get
you sorted, shall we?
Nigel hands Shelby a ROOM KEY.

Settle in. Order room service! It’s
all on us! Get whatever you want.

See you tomorrow for the first leg
of the competition! Oh! And bundle
up, the forecast looks promising,
so you’ll be painting en plain air!

Nigel leaves.
Shelby beams and turns toward the elevators. She passes a man
in a tan peacoat, scarf, and dark sunglasses. It’s giving
‘celebrity hiding from paparazzi.’ Henry. His hair is short,
his face now clean-shaven.
As they cross paths, they’re both suddenly yanked to a STOP.
They stop, look at one another - confused.

Apologies--
They try to pull away from one another, but they’re stuck.
THE STRAP of Henry's art supply bag is caught around THE
BUTTON on Shelby's jacket sleeve.

Attached.
They each step in opposite directions. The strap goes taut.
Careful! This is my favorite coat.
And I’m rather partial to this bag.
Shelby notices the paintbrush sticking out of his bag.
Shelby holds out her not-stuck arm for a handshake.

I’m Shelby.
Henry goes to introduce himself. Stops short - says nothing.

I see. I’m the competition, so
you’re keeping it close to the
vest. Fine. A bit petty, but fine.
Henry remains at a loss for words.

Right, yes, of course--
They both rotate at the same time - in opposite directions.
Now they're even more tangled. And it’s drawn them CLOSER.

Just let me--
Henry gives his bag strap a hard tug.
POP! Shelby’s button flies off. The two stagger back slightly
as they detach. Shelby looks from the button on the floor to
the RIP in her sleeve, then to Henry in accusation.

I’m terribly sorry. I can send it
out for mending.

Nice meeting you, whoever you are.
Your personality perfectly matches
your choice to wear SUNGLASSES
INSIDE.

Shelby turns and leaves. Henry stands a moment, processing,
before he turns and steps up to the reception.

Checking in. I’m part of the Jingle
Bell Paint Off. The name is...Mark.
Mark Masterson.

Shelby steps into her room and brightens when she sees the
breathtaking view of the mountains out the large window.

Shelby reads a card atop a cheeseboard that reads: “Welcome
Shelby! Best of luck! - Nigel Star and the Jingle Bell Paint
Off Team.” Shelby plucks a grape off the cheeseboard.

I could get used to this.
JUMP TO
Shelby inspects her torn snagged sleeve where the loose
threads stand on in, bereft of a button.

She sighs and hangs her ruined coat. She flops down on the
bed, soaking it all in.
OMITTED18 18

Knock, knock, knock.
Shelby opens her door, hair and eye mask all eschew.

Shelby sits facing a mirror, wearing her hotel robe, rollers
in her hair, as MIA(20s), effortlessly cool, paints her face.

This really isn’t necessary. I’m
just a painter. Or, well, I’m more
of a community director who happens
to paint--
Mia spins Shelby around to face her.

You are on a TV show. The make up
and hair is necessary. AND out of
the thousands of people who
submitted to be on this show, you
were chosen. So, you aren’t someone
who “happens to paint.” You are a
painter.
Mia spins Shelby back around to look at herself. Shelby lets
these words wash over her. YOU ARE A PAINTER.

You wouldn’t happen to have
anything to cover up a rip in my
coat, would you?

A small snow-covered hill rises covered with pine trees as
far as the eye can see. Mountains frame the background. At
the base sit several EASELS & CANVASES, looking up a pathway
leading to a barn decorated for Christmas. A CAMERA WOMAN
walks around getting B-Roll.
Shelby steps out of the production van, wearing a peacoat and
a HOLLY & FIR PIN on her sleeve where the button used to be.
She takes in the scene

Contestants, take your place behind
an easel. We roll in twenty.

Shelby stands behind her easel and canvas, in line with the
other artists. She squints at the bright film lights. Henry
steps up to the easel beside her, wearing reading glasses, a
veritable Clark Kent.

Nice reading glasses. Kind of you
to give your sunglasses a break.

Henry laughs, amused. They turn their attention to Nigel who
takes his place in front of the camera.

Camera roll. Sound speed. On in 5,
4, 3, 2–
CAMERA POV:

Welcome to The Jingle Bell Paint
Off. I’m your host, Nigel Star, and
over the next few weeks these six
talented artists will compete for
the chance to display their art in
the prestigious National Gallery
and win $50,000.

Today our artists will paint this
charming scene in just two hours.
Artists ready your brushes! And...
PAINT!
The Camera Woman circles as the artists squeeze paint onto
palettes and wet their canvases. Shelby looks around,
flustered. Frozen. Henry mixes colors, then notices Shelby.

Are you frozen from the winter cold
or nerves?
Shelby snaps to attention.
I’m not-- I’m fine. Great actually.

Great. We wouldn’t want you going
home on day one, would we?
Henry flashes a broad grin. Shelby bristles.

No. We wouldn’t.
She gets to work. A fiery determination in her eyes.
B-ROLL: The artists paint in a variety of styles... abstract
oil paints, watercolors, spray paint, etc. Shelby
concentrates hard as she paints her romantic scene.

Let’s get to know some of our
artists--

Shelby sits in a chair in front of a green screen background.
Something Christmasy.
PRE-RECORDED INTERVIEW:

Oh um. I’m from Philadelphia, born
and raised-- oh ha. Like the song.

Beverly watches Shelby’s interview on the TV in the office.
INSERT - TV:

--I’ve been painting since I could
walk. My mom likes to brag that I
added the finishing touches to most
of the murals in our community Art
Center.

It’s an integral part of the
community. That’s why I’m
competing. So people can keep
enjoying local art. Because art...
it’s for everyone.

Shelby offers a self-conscious smile.
Beverly beams.
Nigel walks over to Shelby and her canvas.

Shelby, talk to me about your
painting style.

Oh, um. I tend to paint more on the
abstract side.

I can see that. And your current
painting has a sort of romantic
quality to it, no?
Shelby looks at her painting. Gets lost in it.

Yeah. I guess it does. This place---
it feels like a magical spot for
two lovers to meet beneath the
falling snow.
Nigel’s eyebrows lift in surprise.

And is there a special someone you
would like to meet here? Someone
back home, perhaps?
Henry glances over. Shelby turns red.

Oh no. No, I’m very single. I mean--
sorry, that makes it sound like I
haven’t-- I’ve had LOTS of
boyfriends. Not LOTS! Just. I’ve
dated--

Well, win this contest and perhaps
there will be! Good luck, Shelby.
Shelby nods in mortification. Nigel moves on. Henry laughs.

I captured what I needed to. No
need to overwork the canvas.
Henry walks away from his station, content.
Would you look at this view!
Shelby shakes her head: focus. She keeps painting.

An hour later, Nigel looks at his wristwatch, then to the
artists.

Artists! You have 30 seconds to
finish your paintings.
Shelby makes one last brush stroke then sets her brush down.
She steps back, observes her work, and nods. That’ll do.

Brushes down! Time for our judges
to make their rounds.
The THREE JUDGES pass by each canvas making marks on their
notepads and murmuring to one-another.
JUMP TO
The artists stand in a semi-circle awaiting the results.

As you know, our three judges score
on several different categories,
making one cumulative score. Sadly,
the artist with the lowest score
will be leaving us today.
Nigel opens an envelope and reads.

The artist leaving us today created
quite a romantic scene--
Shelby sucks in a breath.

However, judges felt their painting
lacked the Christmas spirit evoked
by this wonderful winter landscape.
That artist is...
Shelby closes her eyes, ready to step forward and go home.

One of the artists hangs their head. Shelby opens her eyes in
shock as the artist steps forward to shake Nigel’s hand.

We’re sad to see you go.
Bernard nods sadly, then walks off.

Thank you for watching The Jingle
Bell Paint Off. I’m Nigel Star, and
we’ll see you next time for an
entirely new holiday scene. Be sure
to pencil us in.
The red camera light blinks off. The Camera Woman packs up
her gear. Shelby sighs in relief. Nigel hands score cards to
each of the artists.

Your individual score cards.
Artists find them helpful as they
attempt to improve upon certain
categories each round.
Nigel hands Shelby her score card.

THIS close to the chopping block
Miss Sanders.
Shelby blanches.

Don’t take it too personally.
Nigel hands Henry his scorecard.

As were you Mr. Masterson. Just
barely skated by.

Aw, now. Don’t take it too
personally.
Shelby claps Henry on the back, then walks off.
Shelby sits on the edge of her bed, on the phone to her mom.

title: INT. BEVERLY’S HOUSE - LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

blocks.text:
I only scored one point higher than
the artist who got eliminated
today. The judges said my painting
lacked quality composition.

Art is so subjective, how they can
score paintings is beyond me--

I might as well start packing my
bags now. There’s no way I’m making
it to the finale Christmas gala.

Don’t give up just because you got
one bad score. You need to find
your way back to the joy of
painting. And go have some fun
while you’re at it! Go do things
outside of the competition and get
into the holiday spirit!
Of course I am. I love you darling.

Love you, mom.
Shelby ends the call. She sighs and looks out her window.
It’s so festive outside. She stands and heads for the door.

title: EXT. HOLLYFERN HIDEAWAY - FRONT STEPS - NIGHT

blocks.text: Henry stands off to the side and takes a call.
Father, to what do I owe the--
Henry, where on earth are you?
Henry looks around frantically for inspiration.

Ah well, being King is not without
its distractions. I hardly blame
you for forgetting.

Your secretary does not have any
fundraisers on your calendar until
next year--

That’s because... they moved the
date. Suddenly. And I... wanted to
surprise you by taking your advice,
and getting serious. So, here I am,
in America, at this fundraising
event to... represent Serendovia
and our... culture, the best way I
know how.

Shocked is more like. Right, well.
I expect you to comport yourself
like a royal and to return well
before your coronation.

Ah. Chancellor. Do come in--
George ends the call. Henry sighs and makes his way inside.

Jazzy Christmas Music.
The cozy fireplace area is adorned in garland and white
twinkle lights. Shelby walks in but pauses when she sees the
only other patron is... Henry. She turns on her heel.
Shelby freezes. Turns around. Pretends to just notice him.
Oh. Hello, you. Didn’t see you th--

I don’t have any more bags for you
to steal, but you’re welcome to
sit.

Henry shrugs: suit yourself.
Shelby hesitates for a moment, then sighs. Fine. She walks
over to the sofa chairs and sits in the chair opposite Henry.
Shelby looks toward the fireplace, lost in thought.
Henry watches her.

If it’s any comfort, at least we’re
in the bottom together.

Yeah, not comforting.
Henry passes her his score card.

I reckon you did better than me.
Shelby reviews his card, surprise washing over her face.

I’m not. It’s just, we got the same
exact cumulative score.

Your score card. I showed you mine.
You show me yours.
Shelby begrudgingly pulls hers out and hands it to Henry.

You excelled in quality of
composition, while I--

Excelled in creativity and theme.
The areas I scored lowest. Huh.
Were our skill sets combined, our
scores would be near perfect.
Shelby sits up straight. A lightbulb moment.

We’re competing as individuals. We
can’t share a canvas--

No. No I mean... you have a strong
grasp on composition. I can see
beyond the scene to what isn’t
there. The story. We could help
each other improve our weak spots!
Henry considers.

Interesting. And you’d want to do
that... with me?
Henry laughs and nods. Fair enough.

I’m Hen--Mark, by the way. I didn’t
properly introduce myself before.

Apologies. What do you say, we
start this little experiment
tomorrow?

The town, surrounded by the deep blue winter darkness, shines
like a beacon of light, brilliantly illuminated by Christmas
lights and decor strung about town. We fade out on the
twinkling lights and hopeful-sounding Christmas music.

Henry stands outside near a plethora of kitschy outdoor
Christmas decor, holding two to-go cups. Shelby walks out of
the Hollyfern Hideaway, a satchel of supplies over her
shoulder. Henry holds out the cup of COFFEE.

I wasn’t sure how you like your
coffee--

I... don’t like coffee. Tea gal.
Henry swaps the cup. Offers the one with TEA.

Which is why I... got you tea.
Shelby accepts the cup. Eyes the name on the cup.

Mm. Shall we?
Henry starts walking. Shelby rushes to catch up.

Shelby and Henry arrive at the edge of barn where they filmed
the day before.

You want to improve upon your
compositions, yes?
Henry guides Shelby to an already pre-set easel and canvas.

How is this here!? Did you set this
up in the dead of night!?
Ha... Kidding. I took a cab.

This landscape is rich in
contrasting shapes, objects, and
textures. Not to mention the way
the light catches at different
points. Ideal for a quality
composition.

Of course you do. Apologies. Now,
when you went to art school, what
did you--

I didn’t. Go to art school. I
didn’t study how to paint. I
just... did it. I’ve just kind of
always painted, since I was a kid.

Which explains why your art feels
so free and alive.

BUT when it comes to composition,
we ought to review some technical
basics.
JUMP TO
Shelby holds her brush up to the canvas, waiting.

A quality composition is achieved
by optimizing the positioning of
different elements within your
frame. Juxtaposing smaller objects
against larger objects. Variegating
colors to create atmospheric
perspective. And of course,
balancing soft and hard lines to
create contrast and definition.
Will there be a test at the end?

Take in the environment piece by
piece.
SHELBY’S POV: the tall pine trees. The barn. The snowy hill.
She lightly sketches the larger shapes onto her canvas.

Good. And then sandwich the medium
objects beside larger ones, and the
small beside the medium.
JUMP TO
Shelby’s canvas is painted in. Not finished, but the bulk of
the objects, shapes, and features are there.

Now we refine, add detail and
expressive dabbles.

Your own personal flourish. Oh, and
keep your peripheral margins void
of visual information. You want to
re-direct the viewer to the center
of your canvas. All of which I
reckon you know intuitively, but--
Shelby sets her brush down and looks at Henry.

Are you like, a painting instructor
or something? Because you talk
about ‘atmospheric perspective’
like you’re giving a Ted Talk.

No. But I am required to make
public speeches as part of my...
job. Plus, I received an
outstanding arts education from
many artists of renown--

So, you’re like a trust fund kid
turned CEO then? Traded in your
paint brushes and “outstanding art
education” for stock options?

Let’s just... focus on your
painting, shall we?
Shelby smirks triumphantly, like she’s got him figured out.
JUMP TO

Shelby steps back from her painting and marvels at the
improved composition.
Huh. Would you look at that.

It didn’t hurt that there was no
time limit, or cameras, or gigantic
lights hanging over the space.

Upbeat Christmas music plays as the sun sets on the quaint
bed & breakfast. The Christmas lights twinkle brightly.

Shelby and Henry walk up to the elevator. The elevator doors
open. A person steps out, leaving the elevator empty.
Oh. Uh, I’ll wait for the next one.

Sharing an elevator with just one
other person.

Elevators are intimate spaces,
Mark. It’s one thing if the
elevator is full.

It’s another when it’s just you and
another person you don’t know very
well. And if you don’t have
anything to talk about, it’s just
awkward silence and loud breathing.

Yech. No thank you. I’ll wait for
the next one.
Henry shakes his head and steps into the elevator.

Hope you’re ready for your tutorial
tomorrow. It’s gonna be a doozy!

Henry laughs as the elevator doors shut. Shelby waits a
moment, then presses the elevator button again.

Shelby paints the view outside her HOTEL ROOM window.
[Christmas-y view to be determined by production.]
She sketches the large objects first. Then the medium
objects. Then the small ones.
Shelby looks up from her painting. Thinks for a moment,
smiles, an idea forming.

The next day, Shelby sits on a bench outside the Hollyfern
Hideaway, all bundled up. She holds a drink carrier with two
to-go cups. She listens to a voicemail on her phone.

Shelby Sanders! Is your business
struggling? Is debt weighing you
down? Consider our loan forgiveness
program. We offer cash up front
with just a 6.7% interest rat---
Shelby growls under her breath. Presses DELETE on her phone.

We don’t need your loan forgiveness
you little--

Am I... interrupting?
Shelby startles. She looks up to see Henry.

That’s not concerning at all.
Is one of those beverages for me?

If you like English breakfast. Felt
like a safe bet on account of the
accent.
Henry grabs one of the cups of tea.

English Breakfast is great. But I’m
not English.

Er, just a small country you’ve
probably never heard of-- So, where
will today’s lesson be?
Henry sits beside her. He opens his bag of paints.
What do you propose we paint with?

We aren’t painting today. Today is
about soaking up inspiration.

We can’t tell the full story of a
landscape if we don’t get to
intimately know it and the people
who inhabit it.

We’re people watching.
Henry and Shelby face out, sipping their tea and observing
the view in front of them. Shelby sighs, contented.

Do you do this a lot? Sit and watch
strangers?

There’s your problem. People are
fascinating. People tell stories,
even when they don’t mean to. Like
how they interact with the world
around them. Take her--

Shelby points to a woman across the way, sitting alone,
reading a book and sipping a hot drink from her thermos.

Maybe she comes to this spot every
Sunday. OR maybe this is the first
quiet morning she’s had in weeks.
Henry watches as the woman waves to a passerby.

What does her interaction with the
space tell us? How does it make you
feel?
Henry nods thoughtfully, then notices Shelby waiting.

It makes me feel... a longing for
something. A slower, gentler life.

A life filled with moments where I
have no place else I need to be.
Shelby’s eyebrows raise in surprise.

Wow. Okay. Yes! That’s exactly what
I’m talking about. That is what you
want to put into your paintings.

Alright our next lesson awaits--
OMITTED38 38
Shelby claps her hands together, excited.

For this--
Shelby plops on the ground and makes snow angels.

Is this wise? This may be someone’s
private property.

Ohhh just get down here, Mark!
Shelby yanks Henry down beside her. He lies back.

Make a snow angel. Become one with
the environment. Tell a story.
Shelby kicks her arms and legs out gleefully. Henry self-
consciously and rigidly follows suit.

And what? Be jealous of how much
fun we’re having? Or rather, how
much fun I’m having since you look
like a sad fish flopping around.

You do. You’re making sad snow
angels. I didn’t know that was
possible.
Henry makes more ferocious snow angels.
Now the snow angels are angry.

Now stand up. Carefully! We don’t
want to destroy our masterpiece.
They stand and behold their art.

My snow angel does look rather
aggrieved compared to yours.

But it’s an interesting story I’d
want to paint.

Henry and Shelby walk through the Hollyfern Hideaway to the
elevators once more. Henry presses the button. The door
OPENS.
You take it. I’ll fetch the next.
Shelby smiles, then steps inside the elevator.
Thank you. See you tomorrow on set.

Let us hope these last few days
made a difference.

Here’s hoping.
The elevator doors shut. Shelby sighs. Here’s hoping, indeed.

title: INT. SHELBY’S HOTEL ROOM - THE NEXT DAY

blocks.text: Shelby sits in the HMU chair. Mia curls her hair.

I love to hear it! For what it’s
worth, I’m rooting for you.
Shelby beams at Mia with gratitude.

A quaint church with BELLS atop the belfry. A Christmas
wreath adorns the doors. Snow all around.
Shelby takes in the view. Nigel approaches.

I hope you brought your A-game
today, Shelby!

Me too...
Nigel heads toward the Camera Woman. Shelby takes her place
next to Henry. She frowns at the church.

Hmm? Nothing. It’s just... this
place feels... I don’t know, too
perfect. Almost fabricated? Like a
postcard.

No, it’s just... I don’t know.
Never mind.

Do me a favor? Don’t get
eliminated. Otherwise I might
assume I’m a bad teacher.

You don’t come in last, either.
Don’t go scoring the highest... but
don’t come in last.

As you wish.
Henry winks, then focuses on his station. Shelby looks at him
a second too long. Nigel steps in front of the artists. The
camera blinks red.

Beverly stares up at the TV where THE JINGLE BELL PAINT OFF
plays. She wrings her hands together, nervous.

--to The Jingle Bell Paint Off.
Today our artists turn their easels
toward this postcard-perfect church
and its Christmas bells--
You’ve got this Shelby. C’mon girl!
Shelby shares one last glance with Henry. They nod.

They’ll have just two and a half
hours to capture this
quintessential winter scene.
Artists, ready your brushes. And...
PAINT!
Henry wets his canvas with water. Shelby goes to make her
first composition marks, then hesitates.

She studies the scene for a moment.
FOCUS ON: off to the side of the church, almost out of view,
sit brown donation boxes. Inside, CHRISTMAS YARD DECOR.
With one final look at the church, Shelby pivots her canvas
forty-five degrees, composing the church off to one side and
the churchyard in the foreground.

Finding my story.
Shelby trots off toward the churchyard. Henry stares after
her. He tries to paint the view of the church bells ahead of
him. Sighs. He turns his canvas around, too.
Henry stomps off after Shelby.
If I get eliminated because of you--
I didn’t ask you to follow me--

I had to know what you’re up to.
It’s very distracting.
Shelby grins then stops in the middle of the snowy yard.

Mark. Trust me.
Henry goes to correct her, then stops. Guilt washes over his
face. Shelby grabs one of the donation boxes.
Fine. But then we actually paint.

Obviously.
CAMERA POV: the camera circles the artists still facing the
cabin until it spots motion in the yard. Shelby and Henry
laugh as they arrange the Christmas lawn decor items.

While most of the artists have put
paint to canvas already, two
artists are taking a different
approach entirely.
CAMERA POV: Shelby removes her scarf from around her neck and
wraps it around the PLASTIC SNOWMAN. Henry nods
enthusiastically. Camera zooms in on his face.

Henry sits in an interview chair, a green-screen holiday
backdrop behind him. His sunglasses on.
PRE-RECORDED INTERVIEW:

I can’t. My eyes are... sensitive
to studio lighting?
Beat.
JUMP TO

I am a classically trained painter.
I prefer painting in the style of
classical realism or romantic
realism. Many of my paintings have
been of my family’s garden--

Becks snacks on Christmas sugar cookies while she channel
surfs on the TV. The Jingle Bell Paint Off appears on the
screen. Becks chokes when she sees her brother.

What do I hope to get from being on
this show? I suppose I’d like to
prove to myself... to my family...
that art is instrumental to
society. That art is just as
important as, say, running a
government--
George wanders in, looking over papers.

Is that Henry I hear?
Becks quickly winks the TV off.

No! That would be impossible since
he’s--

In America for that fundraising
event. Right. Silly of me.
Happens to the best of us.

Becks smiles at her father who looks at her suspiciously
before shaking his head.

Right then. What was I-- oh yes--
George traipses out of the room with purpose. Once Becks is
certain he’s gone, she turns the TV back on.

Shelby adjusts a light-up REINDEER while Henry sets down a
classic wooden sleigh. The reindeer is slightly unbalanced.

Hmm...
Henry gives the reindeer a quick adjustment, leveling it.

So you’re saying I just needed a
little more patience?
Here. I think we’ve earned these.

Henry reaches into his coat pocket and pulls out a handful of
wrapped caramel candies - and a lone SERENDOVIAN COIN slips
out.

Aw, you keep hard Carmels in your
pocket like a little grandpa? Cute.

It’s pronounced care-a-mel. And
it’s rather a dignified treat.

Well here in UH-Mer-I-KUH, we call
them car-mulls.
Shelby snatches one of the caramel candies and plops it in
her mouth. Henry laughs.

Serendovia? Is that where you’re
from?

I--yes. It’s a small Country.
Nothing to wax on about really--

I doubt that. I mean, you’re from
there. So that automatically makes
it interesting.
Henry turns to Shelby, unable to hide his wolfish grin.

I didn’t say that. I said where you
are from sounds interesting--

Shelby rolls her eyes. Henry grins, triumphant. Shelby
frowns, looking at their Christmas decor.

Henry removes the red scarf around his neck, and drapes it
around the neck of one of the reindeer. They step back and
observe their strange Christmas scene.

Wow. I can’t tell if it’s bizarre
or beautiful.

An hour later, the artists stand beside their finished
paintings. The other paintings are of the CHURCH BELLS.
Shelby and Henry’s feature the church with the Christmas yard
decor scene.
The judges’ eyes go wide when they see their paintings. They
scribble down notes and whisper to one another.

Suddenly not so confident in our
decision to deviate.
Nigel holds a cue card and addresses the artists.

Remarkable job today artists.
Unfortunately, there are only four
spots in the next heat, which means
one artist will be leaving us
today. In an unusual turn of
events, two of you chose not to
feature the predetermined setting.
Which, according to the rules is...
Shelby and Henry suck in a breath.

Acceptable. Unusual, but
acceptable.
Shelby loosens a breath.

This did make our judges job
significantly harder today. But
they have come to a decision. The
artist leaving us today is...
Shelby grabs Henry’s hand. He looks down in surprise.

Ashley. So sorry Ashley, we sure
are sad to see you go.

One of the artists steps forward, shakes Nigel’s hand and
walks off. Shelby looks down at her and Henry’s hands,
intertwined. She releases his hand like she’s been shocked.

That’s it for today’s episode. I’m
Nigel Star, thank you for watching
Jingle Bell Paint Off! We’ll be
back in a few days as we head into
the quarter-finals. Be sure to
pencil us in

Cut.
The Camera Woman tilts the camera down. Nigel removes his mic
from his lapel as he walks over to Shelby and Henry.

In all my years of filming this
show, I’ve never seen any artist do
what you two did today! It was
absolutely, 100%--

I mean, peak entertainment! Just
the sort of thing this show needed
to liven things up a bit. Brava!

Th--thank you!
Nigel hands them both their scorecards.

Your scores weren’t bad either. Not
bad at all. Keep up the good work!

The Hollyfern Hideaway Christmas lights blink brightly. A
mechanical Santa Clause waves and shouts: “Ho, Ho, Ho, Merry
Christmas!”

Shelby sits at the desk in her red and green plaid pajamas.
She sips a hot cocoa on call with her Mom.

title: INT. BEVERLY’S HOUSE - LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

blocks.text: Beverly sits on her couch with a cup of tea.

--You turning your easel around,
finding your own story, I was
jumping out of my seat!

And the other contestant? The
handsome one!? How did you two
become... friendly?

Oh. Um, Mark and I, we’re helping
each other get to the final.

Kind of like team mates... who are
competing against each other.

Shelby smiles. She can’t even lie. She really does like him.
Beverly catches it and beams. She claps her hands together.
Shelby laughs, shaking her head. No use hiding her feelings.

He’s easy to be around. It feels
like I’ve known him forever. We
just... click. It’s nice.
Was that so hard to admit?
Oh, ya know. Holding down the fort!

Once I win this thing and we’ll get
those repairs done, the art center
will be at full-force--

Or you keep painting.
They face off. Neither budging. Shelby sighs.

I miss you. It doesn’t feel like
December without you. Without our
midnight Christmas cookie bakes.

My favorite. We’ll have plenty more
Decembers together. Enjoy this one
and all it has to offer.

Henry sits on the edge of his bed when the phone rings. A
photo of BECKS pops up on the screen.
Becks! I’m glad to hear your--

BEGIN INTERCUT/SPLIT SCREEN
Henry looks around.
I saw you on the television!

It’s a rather niche show, I doubt
many people have seen--

No. I turned it off before he could
see. But someone is going to
recognize you.

Or should I say “Mark Masterson?”
Those reading glasses are hardly a
disguise, Clark Kent--

Yes. And I know it’s likely to blow
up in my face spectacularly.

But this might be my last chance to
enjoy any kind of life outside the
one that’s been chosen for me.
Becks gives pause.

I may not even make it past the
next round, in which case, I’ll be
home in a few days. No one will be
the wiser.

This IS an extraordinarily absurd
idea--

--And the second someone sorts out
that you’re you, the tabloids will
have a field day, and father the
conniption OF ALL conniptions--

Of course you big numpty. I think
you very well could win this thing.

And if you do, perhaps father will
finally listen... and maybe, just
maybe, we’ll both get to live the
lives we were meant to lead.

No pressure. Just my fate in Mark
Masterson’s amateur hands.
Amateur? A bit more than amateur--

I like her, by the way. Shelby
Sanders from Philadelphia.

title: INT. SHELBY'S HOTEL ROOM - NIGHT - LATER

blocks.text:
Shelby tosses and turns in bed. She looks at the clock.
12:00am. She sits up and throws on her robe and slippers.

Shelby tiptoes quietly down the festively decorated hallway.
She approaches the kitchen door.
INSERT - SIGN ON DOOR: “Dear guests, Happy holidays! Help
yourself to midnight snacks, located on the shelf near the
door. Enjoy!”

She enters the kitchen, flicks on the light - totally empty.
She rummages through the guest snack shelf.

AHH!!
Shelby startles, flinging a snack bag of COOKIES across the
kitchen. Cookies scatter to the ground. She eyes Henry.
Henry picks up the cookies that fell to the floor.

--you have the footfall of a cat.
What are you doing here?

Midnight cookies. It’s a tradition
my mom and I have around the
holidays. I was feeling a little
homesick, and thought, if I can’t
bake with her right now, I could
enjoy the next best thing...
Shelby gestures to the crumbled cookies in Henry’s hands.
And here I’ve gone and ruined it.
Henry offers Shelby the cookie crumbs.

Oh, no thank you to the dirty floor
cookies. I’ll just grab another--
Shelby turns to the snack shelf. No more cookies. She sighs.

Never mind. That was the last bag
of cookies.
Henry dumps the cookies in the trash. Dusts his hands off.
What, here? In the hotel kitchen?

They’ll be none the wiser. Now, let
me see what we’re working with--
Henry rummages around. Opens a cabinet. Then another.
Henry pulls out a miniature WAFFLE MAKER.

You said you were going to make
cookies. That is a waffle maker.

It is!? In Serendovia we use this
contraption to stamp our letters--

I need a waffle maker because I’m
going to make my mother’s famous
Christmas treat. The waffle cookie.

But if we get caught and kicked
out, I’m pinning all the blame on
you. I’ve got a contest to win.
Henry tosses an apron at Shelby.
BAKING SEQUENCE:
- Shelby and Henry tie aprons around their waists.
- Henry cracks one egg into a bowl of dry ingredients. Shelby
cracks the other. She looks over at him, suddenly aware of
their too-close proximity.
- Henry holds up an electric hand-held mixer. Shelby takes it
from him. Begins mixing, at too high a level. Batter flings
everywhere.
- Henry uses a towel to wipe away the batter on his face.
Shelby helps get a spot he missed. Henry watches her with
interest. When they make eye contact, she pauses before
looking away, self-conscious.
- Henry pours the batter into the waffle iron.

I’m still confused how any part of
this is ‘cookie.’

How did your mom come up with a
waffle-cookie, anyways?

Well, waffles are kind of a staple
where I’m from. Greek influence--

The Belgians and Dutch evolved the
waffle into what it is today.

But the Greeks were the first to
make flat cakes between two metal
plates.

Then Medieval Catholic priests in
Europe fed their congregations tiny
waffles for communion and holy
holidays.

So waffles are like an ancient
Christmas treat?

More or less.
The waffle iron beeps.

He opens it to reveal a golden, petite waffle-cookie.
JUMP TO
A mountain of waffle-cookies covers the counter.
Henry holds up two piping bags of icing: one red, one green.

Ooo, festive.
Henry and Shelby ice their waffle-cookies until they are a
swirl of red and green. Then Henry scatters white sprinkles
across both cookies.

And so artistic.
They hoist their waffle-cookies up and cheers. Shelby takes a
bite. Her eyes go wide.

I can’t even explain it, but it
really is a waffle AND a cookie.
Henry smiles at Shelby. Some new emotion in him unlocked.

title: INT. HOLLYFERN HIDEAWAY - KITCHEN - NIGHT - LATER

blocks.text:
Henry tosses a dish rag over his shoulder. Shelby polishes
off one last bowl. The kitchen is clean once again.

Thank you for this. You made it
feel a little bit more like
Christmas for me.

They smile at one another... a little too long. Shelby snaps
out of the moment.
She grabs a plate of the waffle-cookies.
Shelby offers one last smile before leaving the kitchen.

The waffle-cookies sit on her bedside table. Shelby crawls
into bed. She smiles to herself. She goes to turn her lamp
off, but pauses when her phone lights up.
INSERT - PHONE:
UNKNOWN NUMBER: Would you be up for giving me another lesson?
I still feel like I’m not able to put myself on the canvas.
SHELBY: Mark?

INSERT - PHONE:
Henry types: “I need to be honest...” he deletes this.
He tries again: “Funny story, my name is actually Henry...”
He deletes that too. Then: “I am the Crown Prince of
Serendovia, soon to be King...” He sighs. Deletes.
HENRY: Yes.Got your # from the call-sheet. Is that okay?
SHELBY: That’s totally okay. I suppose I could use your help
honing my‘ expressive dabbles.’

Shelby smiles looking at her phone. Waiting.
INSERT - PHONE:
HENRY: Yeah your dabbles do need some work.
SHELBY: (eye roll emoji)
SHELBY: So, tomorrow?
HENRY: It’s a date.
Shelby pauses, her eyes glued to the words: Its. A. Date.
Henry sits on the edge of his bed staring at the phone.

What were you thinking?
Henry types: “By it’s a date I mean--” but stops when Shelby
responds.

INSERT - PHONE:
SHELBY: It’s a date.
Henry relaxes. Smiles.

Shelby sets her phone down, a new sense of excitement. She
sighs contentedly before flicking the lamp light off.

The next day, Henry holds two to-go cups. Waiting. Shelby
walks up with two to-go cups. They laugh when they see each
other.

I fear we’re becoming rather
predictable, Shelbs.

Alright “Marky-Mark--”
Henry considers correcting her but changes the subject.

The barn has been transformed into a cozy, makeshift
Christmas workshop. Evergreen garlands drape the rafters,
strings of warm twinkle lights crisscross overhead, and paper
snowflakes hang from the beams.
Shelby and Henry stand, facing two large pieces of WHITE
BUTCHER PAPER hanging against one of the barn walls.

I thought we could forget the
lessons today actually... and just
enjoy the freedom to create. No
boundaries. No time limits.

Henry smiles and grabs a large paintbrush. He steps over to a
table where there sits several buckets of paint: RED, GREEN,
SILVER, GOLD.
He dips the brush into the red paint and flicks it at the
butcher paper. Green paint SPLATTERS.
Shelby’s face lights up.

FUN! GIVE ME THAT!
Henry hands her the brush and... a BLINDFOLD.

Where’s the fun in knowing how it’s
going to turn out?
Shelby hesitates, then puts the blindfold on.

Shelby and Henry sit beside their now-finished red & green
SPLATTER PAINTINGS.
Nearby a small RADIO plays Christmas music.

Me too. Every Christmas my mum
would insist on doing a very silly
activity with my sister and me.
This was always my favorite.
Yes. Why do you say it like that?

I don’t know. It just feels like a
crucial piece to the puzzle.
Yes. I can’t figure you out.

Henry frowns. It looks like he’s going to say something when
Shelby cuts in:
Was your mom an artist too?

I’m sorry.
Shelby rests a paint-speckled hand on Henry’s arm.

Sounds like your mom--mum-- was
really amazing.

She was. She was the most alive
person I’d ever met. She saw the
potential in everything. Anything
could become a game, a piece of
art, a--

Precisely. She was the one person
who really understood me.

You two would have really gotten
on, actually.

Shelby smiles warmly. They share a moment that stretches on
too long. Shelby looks away, down at her art.

Are my “expressive dabbles” up to
par now?

If I’m being honest? Your
expressive dabbles never needed
improvement.

Did you invite me to make kiddy-art
with you under... false pretenses?

Henry holds his hands up: guilty.
The song on the RADIO changes to something slow and romantic.
They fall quiet. Beyond the barn, snow falls outside. Henry
studies Shelby, then offers her his paint-speckled hand.

Asking you to dance? Yes.
Shelby slips her hand into his as she skillfully pulls her
into his arms, guiding her in a slow waltz. Shelby marvels.

It’s just. You’re making it very
difficult not to like you.

Henry grins as he spins her beneath his arm. Their laughter
fills the barn as they continue to dance.
Henry and Shelby stand inside the lobby, snow in their hair.
Thank you for such a fun afternoon.
They stand smiling at one another for too long.

Right. I suppose I ought to nip up
to my room.
Just be back down here by six.

Shelby gets ready in the mirror. Applies red lipstick.
Fastens a necklace. She leaves the bathroom just as her phone
buzzes on the counter.
INSERT - PHONE
A missed call from MOM. A text pops ups:
MOM: Give me a call when you get a chance. It’s about the
center. Love you.

In the corner nook, in front of the window, sits a small,
undecorated Christmas tree. Henry approaches, wearing a sharp
looking sweater, holding a present. He takes Shelby in.

Don’t you look lovely.
Shelby blushes.
Henry laughs and hands her the present.

Shelby lifts the lid of the present box to reveal A NEW COAT.
She holds it up. Rubs the soft material on her cheek.

Oh my god, this fabric is like
butter. This feels expensive. Was
it expensive? Actually, don’t tell
me.
You didn’t have to do this.
They smile at one another. Too long.
I got you something too. Come on!
Shelby gestures to the barren Christmas tree.

I asked Nigel if they had one
around. Luckily for us, the
production just got this for the
competition tomorrow. But today,
it’s ours. I figured it might be a
good way for you to feel more like
yourself. Tapping into your inner
child by decorating a Christmas
tree.
Henry stands beside the tree. He touches a branch. Smiles.

I can’t recall the last time I’ve
trimmed my own tree.

What, like, your sister does it for
you or something?
Henry winces, shakes his head no. A secret.

... Oh. Your girlfriend, then? Of
course, I should have--

No. No girlfriend. It’s just. My
family has people who do it for us.

You’re like... really rich, aren’t
you?
Henry gives a tight-lipped smile.

Shelby grabs the two steaming HOT COCOAS off the small table
nearby and hands one to Henry, then pauses.
Wait. Does royalty drink hot cocoa?
Henry takes the drink. He forces a laugh.
Henry and Shelby decorate the Christmas tree.

I was thinking about how some of
the best artists in the world are
inspired by travel. How they leave
their imprint wherever they go.
Like we are doing with this tree.
Do you travel a lot then?

I haven’t traveled outside of the
States. Someday, maybe.

Henry picks up his hot cocoa and sits on the sofa chair near
the Christmas tree. Makes a performance out of getting comfy.

My mom started this art center in
Philly. It became an essential part
of the community. When she got sick-
- she’s okay now, thriving actually-
I took over. The community center
is in this historic building, and
it’s very literally falling apart.

What about your father? Is he
around to help?

He passed when I was really little.
It’s just me and my mom. We’re a
good team.
They share a moment.

Is that why you applied to the
competition? To help the art
center?

That’s mostly why. Maybe deep down
I also--

--want to travel the world and
paint?

My whole life all I wanted to do is
paint. But then that dream started
to feel so... impractical.

Before I got selected for the
competition, I was fine letting
that dream fizzle away. But now...

I get it. When the world finally
validates your passion, your
purpose, it gives you hope. Makes
it feel safe to want for more.

Like, maybe there’s a world where I
save the art center and I get to
travel and paint and find--

But no one really gets to have it
all, right?

I don’t know. It is Christmas.
Miracles and all that.

Though, only one of us can win the
competition.
Shelby looks up at their tree.

Shelby rummages around the box of decor. Henry’s hands meet
hers atop the Christmas star. They look at one another.

Shelby nods. They place the star atop the tree, together.
They pause, looking at one another, too close. They slowly
stand back, peel their eyes from one another, and appraise
the tree.

Shelby and Henry hover outside the elevators. The elevator
dings. The doors OPEN.
They laugh but neither step forward to get in the elevator.

Ahem.
Shelby and Henry turn to see Nigel waiting behind them.

Nigel walks past them. Steps INSIDE the elevator. He looks at
them -- then above their heads -- and smirks.

Ahhh. I see why you weren’t getting
into the elevators now.

Nigel points.
FOCUS ON: A sprig of MISTLETOE hangs from the ceiling above
the entrance to the elevator where Shelby and Henry stand.

I’m not even here.
Nigel covers his eyes teasingly as the elevator doors CLOSE.
Henry and Shelby are left standing there ALONE. They look up
to see the mistletoe above them. Then to one another.
That’s not to say I wouldn’t--

I said that’s not to say I
wouldn’t.
Henry takes a step closer to Shelby.
Henry closes the gap between them.

I--
The elevator dings. The doors OPEN once more. The spell
broken.

--should go to bed. Competition
tomorrow.
Shelby slowly steps away from Henry and INTO the elevator.

Right. Right. Goodnight.
The elevator doors start to close when--
Shelby holds the elevator door open.

Perhaps next time we could scrap
the lessons and make it... a real
date. That is, if you--
They smile at one another as the elevator doors close.

Shelby leans back against the wall of the elevator. Her smile
stretching from ear to ear.
Henry stares at the elevator. Sighs wistfully.

Knock, knock, knock.
Henry stirs the next morning.

No thank you.
Knock, knock, knock.

Henry! Open this door!
Henry’s eyes shoot open. He jumps out of bed. Opens the door.
Becks pushes past him into the room.

What in the world--
Becks thrusts a TABLOID MAGAZINE at him. He looks at it.

Flying 7 1/2 hours just to give me
a magazine is a terrible use of
resources, sister.

Becks rolls her eyes. Henry flips the magazine over.
INSERT - TABLOID: A photo of Shelby smiling up at Henry
outside of the Hollyfern Hideaway. Henry is somewhat
indistinguishable behind his sunglasses and hand shielding
his face.
The caption reads: “Possible Prince sighting?”

The elusive Prince Henry of
Serendovia has possibly been
sighted in America with a mystery
woman--

Hardly. They said “possible
sighting.” You can only see half of
my face here. Could be anyone.
Becks thrusts her phone at Henry. He sighs, takes it.

INSERT - PHONE: a SubText thread that reads “The Jingle Bell
Paint Off - Is Mark Masterson Prince Henry’s Long Lost
Twin??” Beneath that, several comments:
- That’s no twin. That’s Henry in disguise. BET! (99 likes)
- Why would a PRINCE be on some lame painting show?(15 likes)
- Maybe he’s abdicated and living his best life! (200 likes)

Luckily, the vast majority of the
public remain unconvinced that any
royal would deign to wear a
disguise, go on a television show,
and live out some fantasy as an
artist.

For now people seem to buy that you
have an uncanny American
doppelgänger who happens to be a
professional painter--

You admit it, you think I’m a
professional?

As am I! Becks... this is not just
about painting anymore.
The two siblings look at one another. Realization hits Becks.

I’ve never felt this way about
anyone. And for the first time in
my life, I feel like I am exactly
where I’m supposed to be. Like I’ve
finally found my purpose. Do you
know what that feels like!?

I do. That’s how I feel anytime
father trusts me to advise. It’s as
close as I’ll ever come to ruling.
Becks and Henry share a look of deep understanding.

I’ll have the PR teams double-down
on damage control. But it won’t buy
us much time. A few more days, if
we’re lucky.

I told him I was joining you at
your “American fundraiser.”

Perhaps it’s not too late to throw
a real fundraiser as a cover!

You’re going to invent a fake
American charity and throw a
fundraising event for said fake
charity in less than 24 hours?
But when you think about it--

Yes, right, no. Being a royal in
disguise on a fake TV show is
enough fibbing for one lifetime.

Shelby gets her hair and makeup done. Her phone buzzes in her
lap: UNKNOWN CALLER.

Shelby hi, it’s Brenda, your mom’s
real estate agent.

She wanted me to send over some
initial specs. I called but she
didn’t answer. I thought I could
relay the info to you since you

I’m thinking we could list for
$450,000, to start, and negotiate
from there.

I’m sorry, I’m confused. What are
you listing exactly?

The historic property? For the art
center? Your mom said she was
contemplating selling so I said I’d
run numbers, did you not--
Shelby hangs up. She dials her mom. It goes to voicemail.

You’ve reached Beverly, I’m
probably covered in paint teaching
a class. Leave a message!

Mom! Please, call me when you get
this. I’m going to save the art
center, okay? Just, promise me you
won’t do anything drastic until I
get back home. I can win this
thing. Please just... let me try.
Shelby hangs up. A new look of determination in her eyes.

Four easels sit in an arc angled toward the beautifully
decorated fireplace. Garland, fluffy stockings, candles, and
holly berries decorate the mantle.
Shelby and Henry choose two easels next to each other. Shelby
is lost in thought.

Yeah, I just-- I need to focus
today. I can’t go home yet.

Shelby looks at Henry. He smiles at her warmly. She softens.
Henry removes his RED SCARF and offers it to Shelby.
Shelby laughs and gestures toward the crackling fire.

It’s a lucky scarf.
Shelby hesitates then drapes it around her neck.
I’ll take all the luck I can get.
Henry steps back to his easel.

There’s uh, actually something I
need to talk to you about after--
Nigel steps in front of the artists.

I hope you’re ready for another
excellent day of painting.

Roll in 5, 4, 3, 2--
The camera blinks red.

Welcome back to The Jingle Bell
Paint Off competition! Four lucky
artists have made it this far. But
only three will continue on to
paint for next week’s live audience
finale and Christmas Charity Gala.
Today our artists will paint this
cozy Christmas fireplace. They have
just two hours. Artists, ready your
brushes. And… PAINT!
All four artists start painting.
Becks, wearing sunglasses and a hat, enters, hiding at the
back. Nigel steps away from the camera and stops beside her.

My word. You look just like
Princess Rebecca of Serendovia!
I get that at all the time.

title: INT. HOLLYFERN HIDEAWAY - FIREPLACE - DAY - LATER

blocks.text:
The Camera Woman circles the artists. Shelby splatters her
canvas with paint. Nigel interviews her.

Shelby Sanders, what inspired you
to utilize this splatter method for
your canvas?
A friend gave me the idea.

Handsome fellow, her friend.
Brilliant painter too.
Shelby rolls her eyes. Nigel looks between the two.

Any more exciting surprises from
the two of you today?

Sure.
Nigel winks. Shelby and Henry laugh.

title: INT. HOLLYFERN HIDEAWAY - FIREPLACE - DAY - LATER

blocks.text:
The completed Christmas paintings sit on the easels. Nigel
addresses the artists.

Exceptional work today artists.
However, only three of you will
earn a spot at the Christmas
Charity Gala live taping finale,
where one painter will be crowned
champion.
Henry grabs Shelby’s hand. She smiles at him.

Sadly the artist leaving us today
is--

HENRY!
Everyone on set turns toward the voice.

No. The person leaving us is Marta.
Sorry Marta.
Marta hangs her head. Aw man.
King George pushes past the cameras and faces Henry.

Henry, you’ve had your fun, now
stop wasting these people’s time
and return to Serendovia at once.
Shelby looks from King George, to Henry in confusion.
Shelby takes this in. Becks watches from the back.

I am to be coronated in two weeks
time.

So you came on a reality TV show
competition? What--why?
This was my last chance to--
Pretend to be someone you aren’t?
No. That’s not--it wasn’t like that-
You lied to me. This whole time?
Everything I told you was real.
Except your name and who you are.
Henry takes a step toward Shelby, reaching for her.

Please, if we could just talk,
privately, I can explain!

I don’t want to talk to you.
Apparently I don’t even know you.

All the time you spent helping me
improve. Was that just some act of
charity? Take pity on the poor
artist girl who’s going to lose her
business?

Goodness no. This is all being
taken wildly out of context--

You know what the worst part is? I
finally let myself feel something
for someone, only to find out that
person doesn’t even exist.

Mark. I HAD feelings for Mark.
Excuse me--
Henry looks to Nigel. Remembers: they’re being filmed.
My sincerest apologies to you all.
Henry walks off. King George and Becks follow.

This has been The Jingle Bell Paint
Off. Tune in next time for our
final episode. Who knows! Maybe
we’ll learn our own Shelby Sanders
is a secret Viscountess.
Henry storms down the front steps. King George follows.
Of all the stunts to pull--

What were you thinking Henry!
You’ve made a mockery of the crown.
Your mother would be--

Henry stops and turns around to find Becks standing behind
their father.

Mother would be proud of you,
Henry.
Henry fights a well of rising emotions. He nods to his sister
in thanks, then turns to his father.

You have made it very clear that I
have no say in my own future. I am
shackled to the crown. But you
needn’t worry, there will be no
further attempts to pursue my own
passions or joy.

Henry continues walking. His father is shook. Becks looks
back toward the Hollyfern Hideaway. An idea forming.

The camera crew breaks down equipment. Henry’s painting still
sits on its easel.

CLOSE ON: The painting, not of the fireplace but of Shelby
painting the fireplace.
Becks grabs the painting and walks off, on a mission.

Shelby sits down on her hotel bed, stunned. She looks at
herself in the mirror and notices Henry’s scarf around her
shoulders. She yanks it off, scrunching it into an angry ball
and throws it across the room.
Her phone buzzes in her pocket.
INSERT - PHONE: It’s HENRY calling - his caller ID is still
labeled in her phone as “MARK.”
Shelby looks at it and then turns her phone upside down. She
lays down on her bed, and curls up.

title: INT. SHELBY'S HOTEL ROOM - DAY - LATER

blocks.text:
Knock, knock, knock.
Shelby’s eyes shoot open. She answers the door.

My girl!
Beverly wraps Shelby in a huge hug.

Mom!
JUMP TO
Shelby and Beverly wear hotel robes and drink hot cocoa.

Are you really going to sell the
art center?
Because you don’t think I can win?

Are you kidding me!? I know you can
win. I bought my best dress for the
Christmas Gala!

The center was my dream. It was
never yours. And maybe it’s time I
let it go.

I want you to experience all that
life has to offer. I was so excited
you signed up for this competition!
Not because you could win a cash
prize. Because it meant you’d be
painting again. And seeing you
paint again--

It’s made me so happy. So, if
selling the business means you’ll
pursue your dreams, then that’s
what I’ll do.

You have taken such good care of me
these last five years. It’s time I
get back to taking care of you.
Now let’s talk about your Prince!

You’re right to be angry that he
wasn’t fully honest with you.

And when you’re done being angry,
ask yourself... if it’s worth
throwing the rest of it away.
I know you care about him--

--and I think he really cares for
you. I also think there’s more to
the story. And you might want to
learn the whole truth before
throwing it all away.

I’m not excusing what he did. I
just... I’ve never seen you like
this, for anyone. You’ve always
been so careful with your heart.

But keeping people at a distance
doesn't protect you from losing
them. Or from getting hurt. It just
keeps you from really living.
Beverly gets up and grabs a large item wrapped in brown
paper.

This was waiting outside your door
when I arrived. It’s addressed to
you. You should open it.
Shelby eyes it suspiciously. Beverly sets the item down on
the hotel dresser. Outside the large hotel window, snow
begins to fall.

Dramatic Christmas music plays.
Snow falls on the quaint town. The Christmas decor blinks
brightly against the darkened night sky.

A few days later, Henry fastens a tie in a full-length
mirror. Becks enters.

Yech not that tie.
Henry glares at Becks in the mirror. He yanks it off and
wordlessly grabs another from his bed.
You can’t give her up that easily.

She doesn’t want to talk to me,
Becks. Whatever it was, it’s over.

I’ve got to meet with the French
ambassador. I don’t have time--

You don’t actually need father’s
permission to abdicate. You never
have. You could just--
I made a promise. To mother.

To look after you and Father. To
keep this family together. To do
good by Serendovia.
Henry looks in the mirror. Becks comes closer.

Henry. You have looked after Father
and I. And as for Serendovia...
well, there’s more than one way to
do good.
Henry looks down at Becks, lost in thought.
Henry stands, waiting. King George enters.

Henry. I was hoping I might catch
you before the meeting.

I know I have been unyielding in my
stance that you ascend the throne--
You are King. That is your right.

Yes. But as your father... perhaps
I ought to take your desires more
to heart.

When I met your mother... I
considered abdicating.
Henry’s eyebrows raise.

She was an artist. She wasn’t
interested in ruling a country.
But... we fell in love. And I would
have done anything for her.

Your mother... wouldn’t let me. She
was the strongest-willed person
I’ve ever met. Stubborn. Like you.

She set her artistic dreams aside
so we could rule together.
Why are you telling me this?

Your mother never regretted her
decision. But... I always wondered
what her life could have been had
she followed her dream.

Should you decide to pave a trail
of your own, you have my blessing.

George claps Henry on the arm. Henry gapes. George goes to
leave but pauses in the doorway.

I like her, by the way, the artist
from America. Reminds me of your
mother.

George smiles wistfully, then leaves. Henry straightens.
Looks at the clock. He knows what he must do.
Henry pulls out his phone. Makes a call.

Ready the jet. We’re heading back
to Hollyfern Valley. Fast as we
can!

Days later, lights are strung around the ballroom. Auction
items arrive. Poinsettia centerpieces are placed on tall
bartop tables.
FOCUS ON: A banner being hoisted up. It reads “The Jingle
Bell Paint Off Christmas Charity Gala & Live Taping.”
Shelby sits facing the mirror. Mia curls her hair.
Looks like someone got a present.
Mia gestures toward the item wrapped in brown paper.
You’re not going to open it?

Wow, that is a whole other level of
self-control I do not have.
It’s from him, right? The Prince?

And you’re not the least bit
curious? What if what’s inside
changes everything?
Not if you leave it unopened.

Shelby nods. Mia sets the curling iron down. She retrieves
the brown-paper package. She inspects the card.

To Shelby, ”My brother may be a bit
of numpty sometimes... but he’s not
so bad. Promise. - Becks.”
Mia opens the package and gasps.

Mia turns the item around.
REVEAL: Henry’s painting of Shelby.
Shelby stares in disbelief. She looks up at Mia.

It might be too late. He’s already
gone.
Girl! That’s what phones are for.

She stands from the chair, suddenly energized. She pulls out
her phone and steps to the side. Dials. It immediately goes
to Henry’s VOICEMAIL.
Shelby’s smile fades. She sags with disappointment.
Shelby sits back down in the make-up chair, crestfallen.

A sign outside the Hollyfern Hideaway advertises “The Jingle
Bell Paint Off Christmas Charity Gala & Live Taping -
TONIGHT!”

A magical Christmas soiree. A large Christmas tree sparkles
at the center of the room. Twinkle lights wrap around
columns. Red poinsettias color the space.
Servers weave through the crowd holding trays of festive
drinks and hors d'oeuvres. The townspeople, dressed in
Christmas cocktail attire, have turned out in droves.
They weave between rows of tables - auctioning off paintings
from the previous episodes.

All auction proceeds go to the
Jingle Bell Paint Off Scholarship
Fund!

How wonderful!
A small stage sits at the front of the room, where the film
lights blaze and the camera crew make final adjustments.

Shelby enters wearing an elegant emerald gown, pulling
admiring glances from everyone in the room.
Beverly, dressed in Christmas tartan, catches up beside her.

You are a professional artist. This
is just another day on the job.
Shelby turns to her mom. Squeezes her hand.

Merry Christmas Eve my girl. Now,
time to show everyone just who
Shelby Sanders is.
Shelby nods and approaches Nigel and the other artist.

Shelby! Good. You’re here.
Unfortunately, Mark--I mean Prince
Henry-- has flown back to
Serendovia to become King.

Don’t hear that every day. But I
suppose that’s good. One less
artist to compete with!
A server offers the group festive drinks. Nigel takes one.

I must say, the hotel has gone
above and beyond for this finale!
There are two easels on the stage.
Your personal paint supplies are
already pre-set. Grab a bite and a
drink and then head to your
station. Camera rolls in twenty!

Shelby sets up her station. She looks over to the empty easel
at her side... where Henry would have been.

If all attendees can take their
places around the stage, our live
taping finale is about to begin!

Shelby looks out from the stage, where the townspeople make
their way toward the viewing area around the stage.

Nigel stands on the steps out front of the Hollyfern
Hideaway.

Happy Christmas Eve, and welcome to
the live finale of The Jingle Bell
Paint Off, coming to you from
Hollyfern Valley's Christmas
Charity Gala. Tonight's charity
auction will raise money for the
Jingle Bell Paint Off Scholarship,
helping support the next generation
of artists.
The live audience clap. Shelby fidgets nervously. She keeps
looking for the doors to see Henry. But he’s nowhere to be
found.

And now, our final two competitors
will paint for the title, a $50,000
prize, and the honor of having
their work displayed in the
prestigious National Gallery.

Today, our artists may paint
anything they wish, inspired by one
simple theme: What does Christmas
mean to you?

Artists - you have three hours.
Ready your brushes. And… PAINT!
Shelby and the other artist dash off to their easels.

Shelby looks past her canvas to the large, excited crowd. She
takes a deep breath. Begins to paint.
JUMP CUT
Shelby’s face in deep concentration. She applies thick coats
of paint to her canvas.
JUMP CUT
The judges view Shelby’s work over her shoulder. Whisper to
one another. Nod. Walk away. Shelby’s painting takes shape.
Nigel approaches Shelby. She sits back and looks at her
painting, as though it might be finished.

Quite the painting Shelby! Am I
correct in assuming you’re ready to
put down your brush?

I... don’t know. It’s missing
something. I just don’t know what.

What is it exactly you are hoping
to capture?

How this place has made me feel.
How the people I’ve met here have
made me feel...

INSERT - PAINTING: Shelby and Henry dance together in the old
barn.
MEMORY FLASHES:
- Shelby and Henry laughing as they splatter paint.
- Henry offering Shelby his hand to dance.
- The two of them laugh as they dance and spin beneath the
string of lights in the barn.
BACK TO SCENE:
I know what my painting needs.

Then get to it because you have...
five minutes left!
Shelby picks her brush back up, total focus.

And who said watching paint dry
couldn’t be exciting!

10 minutes later, Shelby, the other artist, Nigel, and the
judges stand around two easels and canvases covered in cloth.
The audience around the stage await results in anticipation.

Artists. Over the last three hours
you both managed to produce
outstanding paintings that capture
the essential elements of the
holiday season.
Nigel steps up to the first canvas. Removes the cloth.

This painting evoked feelings of an
old-fashioned Christmas. The
texture and cooler colors created a
real sense of atmosphere. You can
almost feel the chill. Absolutely
brilliant!

Nigel steps up to the next canvas. Removes the cloth.
CLOSE ON: Shelby’s painting of her and Henry dancing in the
barn. But now they are framed by the splatter art - infused
with unusually bright colors (a la Mary Blair).

This painting utilized an entirely
unique color palette. It evoked a
sense of playfulness and warmth.
But what stood out the most is the
romantic focal point: the couple.

The joy and love evoked in this
painting remind us what this
happiest season is all about. Being
with the ones we love most.

While both pieces are remarkable,
only one artist will be crowned
winner today. And that artist is...
Shelby closes her eyes in anticipation.

Shelby Sanders, from Philadelphia!
Shelby’s eyes snap open.

Wha--what!?
Shelby stumbles forward, in shock. Nigel offers his hand.

Congratulations Shelby! You are our
official winner of The Jingle Bell
Paint Off!
One judge drapes a blue ribbon around Shelby’s painting. The
other judges clap her on the back: job well done.

Thank you to all our viewers for
watching. I’m Nigel Star, and this
has been The Jingle Bell Paint Off.
Happy Holidays!

Brilliant work. I can’t wait to see
your show at the National Gallery.
This is just the beginning for you!
Nigel walks off. Beverly rushes over.

Beverly hugs Shelby. When she pulls back she notices Shelby
looking toward the doors of the ballroom.
I don’t know what I thought.

Just then... the ballroom doors suddenly open. Paparazzi
flood in behind... Henry. Everyone turns.
Nigel immediately recognizes him.
Cameras back on! Cameras back on!

The room erupts in gasps and whispers. Shelby freezes as
Henry walks straight to the stage.

I know this is your moment, and I
don’t want to take away from it. I
just couldn’t let you think
everything we shared was a lie,
because it wasn’t.

Shelby, everything I told you about
painting and how alive I feel when
I’m creating, every moment you and
I shared together-- that was real.

I don’t expect you to forgive me. I
just needed you to know that
meeting you, being your friend,
changed me. Changed my life.
The crowd turns from Henry to Shelby who stands in shock.

I...
She can’t find the words. Henry nods in understanding.

Congratulations, Shelby. I am so
proud of you.

Henry smiles sadly then leaves. Shelby finds Beverly and Mia
standing together amongst the crowd.

Shelby smiles and rushes off the stage. The crowd parts and
cheers as she pushes past the ballroom doors.
Shelby races down the hall to see the elevator doors closing.

Henry hands his head wallowing, when a hand juts in between
the two closing doors. He looks up to see Shelby prying the
doors open and stepping inside.
The doors close. Henry’s eyes go wide.

I thought you didn’t like sharing
elevators with strangers.

I don’t.
Henry lets those words wash over him.

I wish we could just start over--
Shelby considers this, then thrusts her hand out for a
handshake. Henry stares at her hand, confused.
Shelby Sanders. Nice to meet you.

Nice to meet you Shelby, I’m Henry.
Henry Xavier Argent... the third.

A name like that, you’d think you
were a Prince.
I was until about... 9 hours ago.

Wait, what!? You didn’t, like, stop
being a Prince for me right?
Because I’ve only known you like a
week and half--

Right, no. Exactly.
They both laugh.

I abdicated in favor of my sister.
I never wanted to rule. I’ve only
ever wanted to paint. And I went on
this show to do just that. Paint.
But then I met you. Which
complicated things a bit...
The elevator doors open. Shelby presses the CLOSE button. The
doors close once again.
I wish you’d just told me.

Me too. It just... it felt nice to
be normal for a moment. I got swept
up in it. In you.
I don’t like that you lied to me.

And calling you Henry is going to
take some getting to used to...
but... getting to know you was the
best Christmas present I could have
asked for.
Henry pulls Shelby toward her, eyes full of love.

Paint. And travel. I’ve heard
Philadelphia has an incredible
community art scene.

What a coincidence, I plan to paint
and travel as well.

Serendovia? I’ve heard it’s “a
small country. Not much to wax on
about.”

Whoever said that sounds like a
proper idiot.
Oh he is. But...he’s growing on me.
They lean in close. Romantic music swells.
Any big plans for New Year’s?

Ah now that’s a shame. I was hoping
you’d be my date to the coronation?

I don’t know. I’ve never gone on a
date with Prince.
No Prince here. Just an artist.

I’d love to.
Henry and Shelby kiss. Happily Ever After.
THE END.
